text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis said the 2.2 million litas price tag on the September 5-6 conference of seven eastern European heads of state and the Russian premier was too expensive there was no chance of signing a joint communique.
- Lithuania and Finland signed a visa-free regime during a visit by Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.
- European Union Commissioner Franz Fischler, on a two-day visit to Lithuania, said the EU intends to allocate 1.52 million Ecu to Lithuania for agricultural reforms.

- A lawyer for a Russian journalist held by the Belarus authorities said Lithuania should take up the case of alleged border violations by ORT employees because Belarus claims it received a report from Lithuania about the violations. Lithuania denies it reported any such thing.
- Vilniaus Vodka reported a net profit of 2.7 million litas in the first half of 1997 versus 3.9 million litas.
- Sewing company Shatrja reported a net profit of 1.9 million litas in the first half of 1997 versus 2.78 million litas in the same period last year.
- The securities commission registered the 3.9 million litas share issue of Mazeikiu Nafta, whose share capital now stands at 584.6 million litas.
- Landsbergis said he was concerned about "sophisticated extremism" on Lithuania's political scene.
- Fertiliser producer Litfosa and Marijampole Canned Milk were Lithuania's largest exporters in the first half of the year.
